A real product marketing system keeps the chain connected and lets work compound over time:
Research → Targeting → Positioning → Messaging

That’s what we’re building at Aisepedia.

campaign_name: Boost Post Engagement April 8, 2026 at 12:43 PM
post_text:
Most PMM tools help you make things. Aisepedia helps you run things. There's a difference.
Making things is a one-pager. A battlecard. A launch deck. Things you hand to someone else and hope they use.
Running things is a competitor displacement that changes how your sales team wins. A market expansion your CEO references in the all-hands. A win rate programme your CRO puts in the board pack.
The PME, Product Marketing Environment, is how you get from one to the other.
Five layers. Each one building on the last.
1. Customer Canvas: Find what your customers are actually saying. Common roles, pain points, buying triggers. Not assumptions. Evidence.
Competitor Canvas: Know what your competitors are doing. Their narratives, their positioning, how they're playing the market. So you know exactly where you win and why.
2. ICP Canvas: Stop guessing who you're selling to. Identify your top personas, their attributes, and the segments your data actually supports.
3. Positioning and Messaging: Craft positioning that holds up in every room. A positioning guide and message map your whole team can use, from the sales deck to the homepage.
4. Artifact Library: Every PMM strategy, analysis and content framework you need, ready to execute. You never start a critical piece of work from a blank slide again.
5. Initiative Flows: Launches, expansions, displacements. Fully built initiatives that deliver real GTM impact. The kind your leadership can point to.
This is what product marketing looks like when it finally has the right environment.
Come and see what's inside.
Link in comments.
